# dsh-plugin-builder
**A guarded, in-editor plugin workshop for DeepSeek Harness — a settings tab plus the `cordis-plugin
-development` skill it hands to your agent.**
English | 中文
## What it does
DSH plugins are small Cordis packages: a Host half that registers services, tools or skills, and an
optional browser half that adds UI. Writing one well means knowing the live API of the host you are
running against, not the API from a blog post.
This package puts that workflow inside DSH:
- it registers the bundled **`cordis-plugin-development`** skill globally, so the agent can follow a

guided design → prototype → implement → validate → package → install workflow;
- it adds a **Settin
gs → Plugins → workshop** tab where you describe what you want in one box and pick an engine (Claude
Code mode, Cordis mode, or standard mode); the tab opens a dedicated session with the skill prompt

pre-filled instead of hijacking your current conversation;
- it ships the **scaffolding and validati
on toolkit** the skill calls: `inspect-target.mjs` (read the real host versions), `scaffold-package.
mjs` (generate a buildable package), `validate-package.mjs` (check the package contract), plus the p
rototype contract and validation matrix references.
The tab never installs anything by itself. It creates a session, seeds the prompt, and leaves the co
nfirmation gates to the agent and to you.
## Requirements
- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.5** (Cordis `4.0.5`). The plugin is validated against that line: it ty
pe-checks against the published `@deepseek-ai/*@0.2.1-rc.5` declarations, builds a ModuleLoader clie

nt bundle, and its unit tests run on Node 22/24.
- Node `^22.19.0 || ^24.0.0`.
- A profile that comp
oses the `skills` service (every standard DSH Web/Desktop profile does).

## Use it

1. Open **Settings → Plugins → workshop** (the tab label follows your UI language).
2. Describe the

plugin you want and choose an engine:
- **Claude Code mode** (default) — a dedicated session on the

ost's default agent.
3. Start it. The tab opens a fresh session in the current workspace, places `/c
ordis-plugin-development …` plus your requirement in the composer, and closes itself. It does not se

nd the message for you.
4. Follow the skill's gates: design confirmed first, then implementation, th
en validation evidence, then an explicit confirmation before anything is installed into a profile.
If the selected preset is missing or broken, the tab reports it before creating a session, so you ne
ver end up with an empty session and a silent failure.
## What is in the package
| Path | Purpose |
| `lib/index.js` | Host entry: parses the bundled `SKILL.md` and registers it through `ctx.skills.re

gister()` |
| `lib/client.js` | Browser bundle: `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` closure factory regis

tering the `settings.plugins.tab` surface |
| `lib/client-helper.js` | Shared helper (`placeSkillPro

mptInDraft`, `focusComposerSoon`) exported for other tabs |
| `skills/cordis-plugin-development/` |
The skill itself: `SKILL.md`, the prototype contract, the validation matrix, and the three toolkit s

cripts |
| `lib/types/` | Generated declarations |
## Skill precedence
DSH 0.2.1 already ships a skill named `cordis-plugin-development` with its agent presets. When that
skill is present the plugin keeps it and skips its bundled copy, so load order can never decide whic
h workflow the agent follows. On hosts that do not ship the skill, the bundled copy is registered in
stead. The workshop tab keeps working either way.
## Compatibility notes
- The **plugin runtime** is validated against DSH 0.2.1-rc.5: the registration shape (`name`, `descr
iption`, `invocation`, `source: 'bundled'`, `provider`, `resourceBase`, `path`, `content`) matches t

he 0.2.1 `SkillRegistration` type, and the client injects only shell-provided modules.
- The **bundl
ed reference material** under `skills/cordis-plugin-development/references/` was written against the
0.1.5-rc.2 interface line. The skill therefore tells the agent to call `inspect-target.mjs` first a
nd to treat those references as background, not as an API contract. Read them the same way.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The scaffold/validation tests exercise the toolkit against a **real DSH source checkout**. Point `DS
H_SOURCE_CHECKOUT` at a deepseek-harness checkout to run them; without it that suite is skipped (the
published package has no checkout).
## Known limitations
- The workshop tab only *starts* a session; the agent still needs the session to have the `cordis-pl

ugin-development` skill in scope (it is registered globally, so it is).
- Reference documents are ve

rsion-stale by design (see above) and are scheduled for a 0.2.1 rewrite.
- Generated plugins are ord
inary DSH bundles; installing one is always your explicit decision.
